 Bulldogs set to take on the Warriors
 Ferris football travels to Detroit as they look to break the D2 record for consecutive wins 
 Nolan Matthews , Editor-In-Chief 
 November 6, 2026 
 Photo by: Miles Joseph, Torch Photographer Sophomore quarterback Marcel Jones celebrates against Michigan Tech on Oct. 24. 
 After another hard-fought victory over a ranked opponent in the Davenport Panthers, the Bulldogs have now tied the all-time D2 record for consecutive wins.
 Ferris has tied Grand Valley State’s record of 39 consecutive wins, which spanned from 2005 to 2007, and they now look to break that record against the Wayne State Warriors.
 The Bulldogs first had to go through No.9-ranked Davenport, and they fought Ferris hard. Despite this, the Bulldogs came out with a 23-14 victory.
 Davenport held Ferris to a season-low 259 yards of offense and 23 points; even so, the Bulldogs never lost the lead to the Panthers. Leading 14-7 coming out of the half and putting up nine in the second half, the Bulldogs pulled off the victory.
 Ferris was without sophomore quarterback Wyatt Bower for the second consecutive game. He is still out with an ankle injury. Junior quarterback Chase Carter started the game for the Bulldogs, going 6 for 14 passing for 95 yards and one touchdown, while rushing 19 times for 90 yards and another touchdown.
 On defense, the Bulldogs managed to stifle the person who is arguably the best running back in the country, senior Cepheus Harris. Harris ran 32 times for 162 yards and scored the Panthers’ only two touchdowns on the day.
 Head coach Tony Annese spoke on the three tough victories these past few weeks as they look towards the end of the regular season.
 “It is critically important,” Annese said. “We’ve played a lot of football at this level over the course of the last few years, and at this stage we need to be aware of the health of our bodies and to make sure we’re not overtraining. Because we’re working every day out there to be the best. Consequently, you put too much mileage on the kids, so we just have to make sure we’re fresh.”
 The No.1-ranked Ferris State Bulldogs (9-0, 5-0 in GLIAC) will travel to Detroit at Tom Adams Field to take on the last-place Wayne State Warriors (0-9, 0-5 in GLIAC).
 Wayne State is in the midst of an 18-game losing streak, during which they have been outscored an incredible 839 points to just 213, averaging 11.8 points per game. During the streak, they have been shut out three times, once last season to the Bulldogs and twice this season in back-to-back games against Northwood and Hillsdale. The Warriors’ last win came all the way back on Nov. 16, 2024, where they took down Northern Michigan 30-14.
 Senior defensive lineman Chimdindu Obi spoke about what it’s like for him to return to his home and take on Wayne State.
 “It is a great feeling to be able to play ball in your own city,” Obi said. “Being able to showcase the reason why you left to go to college, show why you are a Detroit athlete, it’s been great and I’m looking forward to it.”
 The Bulldogs will look to secure their record-setting 40th consecutive win against the struggling Wayne State defense, which is allowing 539.1 yards and 49.9 points per game. Ferris will look again to Carter to lead them, who has thrown for 582 yards and seven touchdowns to just one interception, while rushing 65 times for 342 yards and another two touchdowns.
 Sophomore offensive lineman Jaylen Washington spoke about what it means to him to be able to still be undefeated at this point in the season.
 “I would say it means everything,” Washington said. “Still, we just have to take it one day at a time, one practice at a time, and one game at a time, that’s all it is.”
 The Ferris State Bulldogs will face off against the Wayne State Warriors on Saturday at Tom Adams Field at 1 pm.
